fictional: In the third draft, Mara finally tells her sister she is leaving Cleveland before the lease renews.
real: Last night, Mara finally told her sister she is leaving Cleveland before the lease renews.

fictional: The workshop kept asking why Priya hugs her grandmother twice at the ferry dock before boarding without looking back.
real: Priya hugged her grandmother twice at the ferry dock, then boarded without looking back.

fictional: During the table read, Marcus's farewell speech to his unit ran long, so the writers trimmed the part about the shared cigarettes.
real: Marcus's farewell speech to his unit ran long yesterday, and he never got to the part about the shared cigarettes.

fictional: Chapter twelve opens with Noor packing her father's van at dawn, deciding which goodbyes can fit into one driveway conversation.
real: At dawn Noor packed her father's van, deciding which goodbyes could fit into one driveway conversation.

fictional: In rehearsal, the actress playing Ida keeps breaking when she hands over the shop keys and thanks forty years of customers.
real: Ida kept breaking down at the handover as she passed along the shop keys and thanked forty years of customers.

fictional: Playtesters said the moment when Captain Reyes salutes her crew and steps off the ship for the last time needed more silence.
real: When Captain Reyes saluted her crew and stepped off the ship for the last time, the harbor was silent.

fictional: Beta readers flagged the airport paragraph where Tomas waves until his mother disappears past security as too rushed.
real: At the airport, Tomas waved until his mother disappeared past security, and it all felt too rushed.

fictional: My editor's notes say the scene where Lena leaves the church choir after twenty years should end on the unfinished hymn.
real: On Sunday Lena left the church choir after twenty years, walking out during the unfinished hymn.

fictional: The shooting script has Officer Han clearing out his locker, shaking each partner's hand, and leaving his badge on the counter.
real: This afternoon Officer Han cleared out his locker, shook each partner's hand, and left his badge on the counter.

fictional: According to the outline, Sana's last shift at the diner ends with her taping a thank-you note beside the coffee machine.
real: Sana's last shift at the diner ended with her taping a thank-you note beside the coffee machine before locking up.

fictional: The storyboard shows you waving from the train window while your brother jogs alongside the platform until it ends.
real: You waved from the train window while your brother jogged alongside the platform until it ended.

fictional: In the writers' room we argued whether Grandpa Cyrus should say anything at all when the family car pulls away from the farmhouse.
real: Grandpa Cyrus didn't say anything at all when our car pulled away from the farmhouse on Saturday.

fictional: For the audio drama, Yuki's goodbye to her roommate happens entirely through a closing door and two suitcase zips.
real: Yuki's goodbye to her roommate happened entirely through a closing door and two suitcase zips.

fictional: The final act strands Beatriz at the bus depot, rehearsing the words she will use to end the engagement.
real: Beatriz stood at the bus depot on Friday, rehearsing the words she would use to end the engagement.

fictional: In the final installment of my fanfic, Wren returns the borrowed telescope, bows once, and leaves the observatory without a word.
real: Wren returned the borrowed telescope tonight, bowed once, and left the observatory without a word.

fictional: Fifty thousand words into the novel, my protagonist Aoife finally quits the bakery, apologizing to the ovens like old friends.
real: Aoife finally quit the bakery on Monday, apologizing to the ovens like they were old friends.

fictional: The last panel of issue nine shows Detective Ives leaving the precinct with a cardboard box and no forwarding address.
real: Detective Ives left the precinct at noon with a cardboard box and no forwarding address.

fictional: The stage directions ask Omar to fold his apron slowly before telling the kitchen crew he is moving back to Tunis.
real: Omar folded his apron slowly at closing time before telling the kitchen crew he is moving back to Tunis.

fictional: In the visual novel's true route, Katya releases the rescue dog to its new family and watches the gate swing shut.
real: After breakfast, Katya released the rescue dog to its new family and watched the gate swing shut.

fictional: The audition sides cover the moment Ruth tells her carpool that Friday is her last ride after eleven years.
real: On the highway, Ruth told her carpool that Friday is her last ride after eleven years.

fictional: The short story closes with Anselm shaking the harbor master's hand and sailing the trawler south for good.
real: Anselm shook the harbor master's hand at first light and sailed the trawler south for good.

fictional: Our pilot's cold open follows nurse Dalia hugging each coworker at the station desk as the night shift ends forever.
real: Nurse Dalia hugged each coworker at the station desk as her final night shift ended.

fictional: The second-act number gives Federico eight bars to kiss his daughter's forehead and board the ship to Buenos Aires.
real: Federico had barely a minute to kiss his daughter's forehead before boarding the ship to Buenos Aires.

fictional: My critique group wants more weather in the passage where twins Ada and Aggie split the record collection and part ways.
real: Under Tuesday's drizzle, twins Ada and Aggie split the record collection and finally parted ways.

fictional: Even in the galley proofs, Mrs. Okafor's retirement assembly speech ends mid-sentence, the gymnasium doors already open.
real: Mrs. Okafor's retirement assembly speech ended mid-sentence today, the gymnasium doors already open for the buses.

fictional: In the epilogue, Hugo still sets two coffee cups on the counter each morning, three months after Marisol's funeral.
real: Hugo still sets two coffee cups on the counter each morning, three months after Marisol's funeral.

fictional: The sequel opens with Tess donating her husband's winter coats and keeping only the one that still smells like cedar.
real: Over the weekend Tess donated her husband's winter coats, keeping only the one that still smells like cedar.

fictional: My one-act follows Gideon reading the vet's sympathy card aloud to an empty leash hanging by the door.
real: Gideon read the vet's sympathy card aloud after dinner, the empty leash still hanging by the door.

fictional: In our campaign, Sylvie the bard keeps stopping mid-song on her late mentor's lute, and the whole table goes quiet.
real: Sylvie keeps stopping mid-song on her late mentor's mandolin, and the whole kitchen goes quiet.

fictional: The voiceover explains that Deshi mowed his brother's initials into the lawn the first summer after the accident.
real: Deshi mowed his brother's initials into the lawn this summer, the first one after the accident.

fictional: Page forty of the graphic novel shows Imani wearing her grandmother's church hat to the empty pew, saying nothing.
real: Imani wore her grandmother's church hat to the empty pew at yesterday's service and said nothing.

fictional: For the fiction assignment, I gave my narrator a divorce, a half-packed garage, and a wedding album she cannot throw out.
real: Since the divorce, my garage is half packed, and the wedding album sits in a box I cannot throw out.

fictional: Episode six of the podcast serial finds Bruno replaying his father's last voicemail while the pasta water boils over.
real: Bruno replayed his father's last voicemail again at midnight while the pasta water boiled over.

fictional: In the reprise, Odette's lullaby returns a key lower, sung to the nursery she and Sam finally repainted.
real: These days Odette hums the lullaby a key lower, in the nursery she and Sam finally repainted.

fictional: The trilogy ends with Kofi finishing his mother's crossword in pen, the way she never let him do.
real: This morning Kofi finished his mother's crossword in pen, the way she never let him do.

fictional: The screenplay treatment has Coach Whitaker locking the gym alone after the team's program is cut, banners still up.
real: Coach Whitaker locked the gym alone after the board's vote cut the program, the banners still up.

fictional: Every branch of the interactive story returns to Nadia coming home from the funeral to find her houseplants dying.
real: Nadia came home from the funeral last week to find her houseplants dying.

fictional: The character bible notes that Ansel keeps his late wife's reading glasses in the truck's cup holder, lens-side up.
real: Ansel keeps his late wife's reading glasses in the truck's cup holder, lens-side up, even now.

fictional: The telenovela's widow, Doña Ines, waters the lemon tree at dusk and talks softly to the man who planted it.
real: At dusk, Doña Ines waters the lemon tree and talks softly to the man who planted it.

fictional: Recording the audiobook, the narrator paused at the line where Solomon folds the flag from the coffin into a triangle he cannot put down.
real: At the graveside, Solomon folded the flag from the coffin into a triangle he could not put down.

fictional: Halfway through the novella, Petra finally deletes the group chat from the restaurant that closed, then undoes it.
real: Petra finally deleted the group chat from the restaurant that closed, then undid it before bed.

fictional: In the verse play, Mireille recites the recipe for her aunt's plum dumplings to keep the kitchen from feeling smaller.
real: From memory, Mireille recited her aunt's plum dumpling recipe to keep the kitchen from feeling smaller.

fictional: The animated short shows Barnaby teaching the new apprentice with his old partner's chalk still on the blackboard.
real: Barnaby taught the new apprentice on Wednesday with his old partner's chalk still on the blackboard.

fictional: The director's cut restores the moment Halima renews her brother's library card a year after he went missing.
real: Halima renewed her brother's library card at the downtown branch, one year after he went missing.

fictional: The story I submitted to the magazine ends with rain falling on the lot where June's greenhouse was torn down.
real: Rain fell before sunrise on the lot where June's greenhouse was torn down.

fictional: The bottle episode traps Uncle Rafael in the attic, sorting his son's baseball cards into piles he keeps reshuffling.
real: Uncle Rafael spent the afternoon in the attic, sorting his son's baseball cards into piles he kept reshuffling.

fictional: My flash fiction piece is just Greta returning the borrowed casserole dishes, one porch at a time, after the funeral guests left.
real: Greta returned the borrowed casserole dishes, one porch at a time, once the funeral guests had left.

fictional: One side quest asks the player to help old Fen rebuild the orchard the storm took, sapling by sapling.
real: All spring, old Fen has been rebuilding the orchard the storm took, sapling by sapling.

fictional: The pages I am ghostwriting describe Beata paying for two symphony seats all winter, one of them always empty.
real: All winter Beata paid for two symphony seats, one of them always empty.

fictional: The prologue lingers on twelve-year-old Milo relearning to ride without his grandfather jogging behind the bicycle.
real: This week Milo is relearning to ride without his grandfather jogging behind the bicycle.
